cells.rule: K3.1: "store into an `owned` field or owning-collection slot, including through a `set(owned)` accessor" | §28.6: "A **freshly-produced owned value** — a `new` expression, a call returning `owned T`, a `move` expression, or an owned operator result — stored into a non-`owned` (borrow) field is an **error**" | K3.13: "An **unmarked read of a class-typed binding never consumes**" | §28.3: "An indexer assignment of such a value is not reached by this bullet: it is a call of the indexer's setter, or a"
cells.cite: §28.3 (K3.1, K3.13, field-store bullet cl.2–3, property-store bullet), §28.5, §28.6, §28.7, App. C.3
cells.note: Into an `owned` field, or through `set(owned)`: a marker-free consume. The new holder disposes it on overwrite or teardown. Into a non-`owned` field or property: a fresh or `move`d value is rejected. An unmarked owned binding is a borrow of a scope-bound binding, so clause 2 rejects it. Through a user-declared indexer setter, a fresh temporary or scope-bound borrow is admitted at the call under clause 3's residual (it dangles past its boundary; the K4.1 backstop catches the use). This is an explicit, recorded asymmetry with property stores.

cells.note: A `static owned` (readonly) field takes the value under K3.1 and disposes it at program exit. An overwrite never disposes. An unmarked owned local is a borrow of a scope-bound binding and is rejected. No borrow arises, so nothing outlives a source.

cells.rule: §28.3 property-store bullet (static): "a class- or interface-typed borrow is admitted where the field-store bullet admits it, under its residual and domain clause" | §28.3 cl.4: "The caller-side obligation includes **not transferring the source's object to another domain**" | §30.14: "**no mutable state is ever reachable from two domains.**"

cells.note: A plain-parameter-sourced borrow stored into an admitted mutable static (`Mutex?`, `Task<T>?`, …) is admitted by the field-store bullet's residual (`static readonly` is reachable only from static init, where locals are rejected). The residual and domain clause bound only an object holder and a transfer of the source. Process-global storage publishes the borrow to every domain with no transfer, and no text bounds the owner domain's disposal against another domain's use. Form (ii)'s ground ('every stored task remains independently awaitable') assumes a discharged, process-lived referent.

root_causes.statement: A standard-library generic member that retains a value of its type parameter past the call (TaskCompletionSource<T>.SetResult/TrySetResult, Task.FromResult<T>) is exempt from §9.7's per-instantiation requirements by §3.6 rule 2, and no instantiation-site rule bars a T that holds borrows, so a record, inline array, choice or span carrying borrows is retained in a task with no bound.
root_causes.fix: Add a §30.5 row (and the matching stdlib §6.6/§6.7 restriction): `Task<T>`, `TaskCompletionSource<T>` and `Task.FromResult<T>` at a T that holds borrows are admitted by no row, a compile error at the instantiation site as the move-only row is, `CancellationToken` excepted under A10.

root_causes.statement: Set-erasing positions are reached only 'by implicit conversion', so an explicit `f as Object` yields an Object-typed value that no function-value rule reads (holders key on static type), letting a capture-bearing closure into fields, collections, Object parameters and ref locations; the borrow-erasing twin in §9.7 already lists `as`.
root_causes.fix: Add 'or by an `as` (§17.4) at `Object`' to the set-erasing reach list (and to App. C.1's set-erasing row), so the conversion is the compile error at the `as`, mirroring §9.7's borrow-erasing bullet.

root_causes.statement: A class-typed borrow stored into an admitted mutable static (form (i)/(ii)) is admitted under the field-store residual, but the domain clause bounds only transferring or consuming the source, not publishing the borrow itself to every domain, and K4.3's recorded set has no static-held clause; the owner domain's disposal can race another domain's use, where the flag backstop is not reliable.
root_causes.fix: Rule that a store of a class- or interface-typed borrow into a mutable static admits only a static-storage source (and fresh producers, which the store discharges), rejecting plain-parameter and receiver sources at the site, consistent with App. C.1's reference-free rule for the always-live holder.

root_causes.statement: A captured local or parameter of a value type that holds borrows (or declared IReadOnlySpan<TElement>) contributes no source: provenance clause 1 omits it, and two passages say it 'contributes nothing'. So any route that reads a closure's set (invocation, frame, scoped admission) loses the record-carried borrow.
root_causes.fix: Add 'a captured local or parameter of a value type that holds borrows (or declared IReadOnlySpan<TElement>): the sources of the borrows it carries' to provenance clause 1, and narrow the Deferred-activation 'value-typed capture contributes nothing' and §28.14 bound 1's exemption to value types that hold no borrows.

root_causes.statement: The plain-argument and value-element rows of Domain.Spawn and Parallel constrain `A`/`R` by `sendable, notnull`, which admits sendable classes, while §30.14 requires class-typed crossings to be owned moves.
root_causes.fix: State in stdlib §6.8/§6.12 (and §30.14's call-site list) that an instantiation of a plain `arg: A`, `items: Array<A>` or plain `R` row at a class type is rejected at the call site, re-read per instantiation under §3.6 rule 2, and drop 'the where clauses state the full requirement'.

root_causes.statement: Span-carried borrows have no per-access flag, yet the kernel treats them as flag-backstopped where K5 cannot see them: iterator frames (K6.4 records only the task settlement clause) and, per S1, site-announced kills (K5(ii) admits only two failing shapes).
root_causes.fix: Make a local holding an iterator frame a live local borrow of its carried sources for K5.5 (so moving them is frozen), and add 'a span-carried surviving borrow' as K5(ii)'s third failing shape so a site-announced Dispose of a span's source is frozen while the span or frame is live.

root_causes.statement: §28.14's class/interface `scoped` admission claims 'fully static, no residual trust', but it admits sources reached through `this`, parameters, fields and getters, whose referents a field overwrite can kill under K5.6's runtime-checked posture.
root_causes.fix: Record the field-slot overwrite as a K4.3 residual of the storage-bounded admission (flag-backstopped) and strike 'no residual trust' and K5.7's 'not an admissible backstop' for non-local sources. Alternatively, admit only local, frozen sources at `scoped`.

root_causes.statement: In an async body, `return x;` of a named owned binding under OwningTask<C>/Task<C> is in no consume-table row (K3.2 names Task-family returns only in non-async bodies).
root_causes.fix: Extend K3.2 with 'or, in an async body, under an OwningTask<T> or class-T Task<T> return type, of the result expression' as a marker-free consume.

root_causes.statement: §30.5's closed list of three Pattern A result-slot kinds has no slot for a non-await borrow `return` (receiver-sourced) in an async Task<C> body, so its bound and teardown are unstated.
root_causes.fix: State that a non-await borrow return in an async Task<C> body is rejected (remedy: return a fresh owned value, or `return await` a borrowed task as kind 3).

root_causes.statement: It is unstated whether §9.7's 'read IReadOnlySpan<TElement> as the span' redirect reaches the announcement table's declared-type keying (row 4 static rejection vs row 7 plus §9.7's 'admissible at every member kind').
root_causes.fix: Add one sentence to §28.3 Factory methods saying whether an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` static return is row 4 (rejected at the declaration) or row 7.
